tools.name: RemoteSensingMannKendallTest
tools.description: Tie-corrected original or seasonal Mann-Kendall trend test with an explicitly scaled Sen slope. 趋势显著性与季节性趋势检验。

items.description: Finite observation in value_unit; nulls are not accepted.

x.description: Ordered equally spaced observations. Missing samples must not be silently dropped.

method.description: Tie-corrected MK; seasonal compares matching seasons. Neither profile corrects serial dependence.

period.description: Samples per seasonal cycle; required only for seasonal. At least three complete cycles.

sample_interval.description: Positive spacing between adjacent observations, expressed in time_unit.

value_unit.description: Physical unit of input values, e.g. ppm, mg/kg or dimensionless. Not inferred or converted.

time_unit.description: Unit of sample_interval, e.g. year or month; slope is returned per this unit.

period.description: Samples per cycle, or null for original MK.

significant.description: Whether the asymptotic two-sided test rejects the no-trend null at alpha.

p_value.description: Asymptotic two-sided p-value, not an exact small-sample probability.

slope.description: Sen slope scaled to value_unit per time_unit, not per seasonal cycle.

value_unit.description: Physical unit of input values, e.g. ppm, mg/kg or dimensionless. Not inferred or converted.

time_unit.description: Time unit for the returned slope.

sample_interval.description: Original spacing between samples in time_unit.

warnings.description: Scientific limitations and diagnostic warnings; do not remove them from interpretation.

metadata.input_format: Object conforming to input_schema. Units, defaults and cross-field rules are specified in the schema and source checks.
metadata.output_format: Structured object conforming to output_schema. Direct calls raise ScientificToolError with code/retryable; Agent execution uses its standard error envelope.
limitations: Regularly spaced finite one-dimensional observations; no silent omission of missing samples.
Original and seasonal methods do not correct serial correlation; significance is not causality.
Asymptotic normal p-values are approximate for small samples.
Seasonal mode requires an explicit period and at least three complete cycles.
